about: The moth's hiking wings (docs/moth-3): two racks of carbon tube out to the class's 2.25 m beam (rule 6.2: the racks count), each a frame of a front bar, a rear bar and an outer rail laced with a tight mesh deck the sailor sits and hikes on. Game frame for x (forward from the hull's middle, metres), y outboard from the centreline; z is the hull's deck edge at the root, rising by the dihedral toward the tip. Shape read by eye from the PD/CC BY photos (refs.json: the flying bow-quarter and windward-heel shots show a swept, roughly trapezoid frame with a dark mesh deck): nothing traced.

root.note: where the bars meet the hull's deck edge: the front bar just aft of the mast step (x 0.70), the rear bar near the transom. Milestone A lengthened the wings from 1.3 m at the root (0.15 to -1.15): every photo shows them running from the mast nearly to the transom

tip.note: the outer rail's ends; the corners rounded so the sailor's legs slide over them in a tack

dihedral_note: Milestone A raised it from 5 degrees: the photos show the wings rising outboard, their tips about 0.2-0.3 m over the deck edge. Milestone B kept 14 degrees and added a diagonal strut under each bar from the hull's side: nine reviewers over three rounds read the wings as flat plates at deck level where the photos show frames rising outboard on braces, but at 20 degrees the wing's front tip moved from 2 to 6 px off the camera-matched photo (the near wing in the photos is raised by the boat's heel)

mesh.note: the deck: a tight mesh laced inside the frame, sagging a little in the middle

shroud_note: the shroud base is 1.5 m (the tuning guide's 1,500 mm): each shroud's chainplate sits on the front bar 0.75 m out (socket ShroudBase_L/R, slice 4)

strut.note: the diagonal braces under the front and rear bars: from halfway down the hull's side up to the bar a little past halfway out (Milestone B)
